of zeroes in the denominator .

Understanding Decimal Place Value

Decimals are the natural extension of the Indian place value system to represent decimal fractions (1/10, 1/100, 1/1000) and their sums. For example, 27.53 refers to a quantity with 2 Tens, 7 Units, 5 Tenths, and 3 Hundredths.

Converting Fractions to Decimals

When converting fractions like 1/10, 1/100, or 1/1000 into decimals, the denominator determines the number of decimal places. For instance, 254/1000 equals 0.254.

Dividing by Powers of Ten

To divide any number by a number of the form 1 followed by zeroes (10, 100, 1000), move the decimal point in the dividend to the left by the same number of places as the number of zeroes in the divisor. Add leading zeros if necessary.

Understanding Decimal Place Value

Decimals are the natural extension of the Indian place value system to represent decimal fractions (1/10, 1/100, 1/1000) and their sums. For example, 27.53 refers to a quantity with 2 Tens, 7 Units, 5 Tenths, and 3 Hundredths.

Converting Fractions to Decimals

When converting fractions like 1/10, 1/100, or 1/1000 into decimals, the denominator determines the number of decimal places. For instance, 254/1000 equals 0.254.

Dividing by Powers of Ten

To divide any number by a number of the form 1 followed by zeroes (10, 100, 1000), move the decimal point in the dividend to the left by the same number of places as the number of zeroes in the divisor. Add leading zeros if necessary.
